$comment: THE LIST CI RUNS, not a description of one (#396, stage 1).
scripts/run-checks.mjs iterates this file and ci.yml invokes that runner, so an entry
here IS an execution. A declared list CI did not iterate would be a second source of
truth and worse than the YAML it replaced: it would report a set nobody ran.
Each entry runs its PROOF first and its CHECKER second, in one process, because a
checker whose proof did not run is a checker nobody has watched fail. That ordering was
previously spelled out in six separate `pnpm <name>` scripts chaining `&&`; it is now a
property of the runner, so it cannot be forgotten on the seventh.
STAGE 1 covers only the six that already had the proof-first form. The other 45 checker
steps in ci.yml keep their own steps and pairing keeps parsing YAML for them.

checks.name: route-stubs
checks.why: a route stub matching more than one real endpoint answers requests it was never written for (#379)

checks.name: fixture-premises
checks.why: a fixture that plants into a directory-owned glob must say so, or a reparent leaves it green about nothing (#375)

checks.name: manifest-coupling
checks.why: rung coupling that travels through the generated types (#374)

checks.name: langfuse-wiring
checks.why: observability wiring present in every backend, not only the one someone tested

checks.name: github-reporter
checks.why: a failing e2e job names the test that failed (#362)

checks.name: run-axes-parity
checks.why: the run axes agree across backends rather than each backend deciding separately

checks.name: required-contexts
checks.why: branch protection names required checks in a second place, and a rename makes the two disagree in silence in one direction and in permanent deadlock in the other (#404)

checks.name: undeclared-reverts
checks.why: a branch can undo merged work with every pre-merge gate green, because a revert is self-consistent — its tests are reverted with its code (#406)

checks.name: coverage-surface
checks.why: a shared surface covered only by rung-owned specs loses its tests to an eject while keeping the feature (#373)

checks.name: overrides-inert
checks.why: an override carrying a version selector stops applying once a resolution rises above it, and reads as protection while doing nothing (#378)

checks.name: merge-keeps-registrations
checks.why: two branches appending to one registration list conflict, and taking either side wholesale drops the other's entry — for this very file that means a checker that never runs (#467)

checks.name: barrel-type-exports
checks.why: a type-only export dropped from the barrel is invisible to the runtime completeness guard and still compiles, so tsc is silent and the break surfaces at a consumer (#446)

checks.name: parity-tsconfig
checks.why: a cross-package suite excluded from the package program and absent from the parity include is in NO program: green, and never typechecked (#430)

checks.name: testmatch-anchored
checks.why: an unanchored testMatch means 'this spec' to a reader and 'any path containing this substring' to the engine, so a suffix-named file joins a project silently and runs against the wrong app (#475)

checks.name: e2e-partition
checks.why: a spec gaining or losing a project changes what it is tested against and reports the same green; emptiness checks cannot see it because the spec still runs somewhere and the project still runs something (#475)

checks.name: swallowed-evidence
checks.why: vitest's default reporter swallows console output from a PASSING test, so a check that names its subject with console.log prints nothing and looks exactly like one that never named it (#456)

checks.name: behavioural-evidence
checks.why: a behavioural requirement closed by an existence check reads as satisfied while the behaviour is absent — ADAPT-05 said the run pauses and was satisfied by three exports and a test count (#453)

checks.name: board-declarations
checks.why: the v2.0 label and the v2.0 milestone are two declarations of one fact; when they drift the milestone-filtered board reads as shippable while the label view does not, and the drift has recurred three times (#410)

checks.name: verdict-tokens-disjoint
checks.why: a selftest fixture's verdict printed in the real format, on the same stream in the same job, reads as a real transport defect — and a fixture PASS would read as a clean transport (#496)

checks.name: rung-witnesses
checks.why: a rung no severability cell removes has never been shown severable, and every cell stays green because each one only speaks about its own removals (#495)

checks.name: playwright-history
checks.why: captureGitInfo.diff defaults ON under CI and depth-fetches the PR base into the workspace, so every later history read sees one commit and every file as added there — silently, in whatever tool runs next (#470)

checks.name: graph-id-agreement
checks.why: rung 4's multi-graph fixture copies rung 5's graph ids as literals -- correctly, since reading that file would break an ejected fork -- so nothing stops an upstream rename leaving the fixture green about a backend that no longer exists (#454)

checks.name: graph-list-doc-claim
checks.why: the docs a person reads to decide what upstream registers restate its graph list in prose; deriving it is not available -- the repo already generates one such sentence from a hand-maintained template, which moved the copy rather than removing it (#468)

checks.name: workflow-event-matrix
checks.why: a fork inherits the workflows, so E2E-05's claim about which jobs run on which events -- and skip on fork PRs -- is a claim about what a forker gets; the absence half is satisfied by a workflow where those jobs run for nobody, so presence is asserted with it (E2E-05, CI-01)

checks.name: readme-vocabulary
checks.why: the README's vocabulary table is a second declaration of the manifest's field set, and prose does not run (#487)

checks.name: fork-python-imports
checks.why: a SHARED python test importing a RUNG-OWNED module collects fine in the full tree and dies with an ImportError in every fork below that rung; ruff --select F821 and the boot check are both structurally blind to it (#565)

checks.name: formatted
checks.why: this repo has checkers and tests that parse source TEXT, so whitespace is an input to a verdict rather than a matter of taste — a re-indent already made a parity reader find nothing (#463). Scoped to the files a branch changed: the 651-file backlog (at 8c9172bf) is cleared separately under #406's detector, because a repo-wide reformat is the one diff nobody reads line by line (#405)
